extracted.intended_audience: accountants, corporate counsel, and preparers of SEC filings for investment companies and registrants involved in business combinations (e.g., fund acquisitions, SPACs)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing SEC financial and disclosure requirements when registrants undertake business combinations (fund acquisitions, reverse acquisitions/recapitalizations, shell/ SPAC transactions), including when to file supplemental, predecessor, carve-out, abbreviated, or full financial statements and related Form 8-K/Form 20-F obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental financial information under S-X Rule 6-11(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplemental financial information is provided for an acquired (or to be acquired) fund in lieu of pro forma financial information. This includes information on fees; expected material changes in the acquired fund’s investment portfolio; and material differences in accounting policies between the acquired fund and the investment company registrant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a fee table, an SOI (statement of investments) of the acquired fund modified to reflect material changes in the portfolio due to investment restrictions and narrative disclosure describing such changes, and narrative disclosure about material differences in accounting policies. See S-X Rule 6-11(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee table requirements and format guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: S-X Rule 6-11 does not prescribe a specific format for the fee table; it refers to the format prescribed in the ‘appropriate registration statement’ under the 1940 Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the format in Form N-1A for open-end management investment companies (Item 3 Risk/Return Summary: Fee Table) and Form N-2 for closed-end management investment companies (Item 3 Fee Table and Synopsis). Apply the relevant item and instructions on those forms when preparing the fee table required under S-X Rule 6-11(d)(1)(i).

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of investment restrictions and resulting portfolio changes
rubrics_metrics.description: An acquired fund’s investment portfolio may be impacted by investment restrictions of the investment company registrant. If so, an SOI of the acquired fund is presented in a modified format to reflect the resulting changes in investment holdings and accompanied by narrative disclosure describing the change. [S-X Rule 6-11(d)(1)(ii)]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide examples (e.g., aggregated positions that exceed single-investment limits requiring divestiture) and explain the anticipated divestiture and its impact; include modified SOI and narrative explaining material changes caused by investment restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staff views on pro forma fee and capitalization tables when multiple outcomes exist
rubrics_metrics.description: Merger transactions with multiple target funds can lead to multiple pro forma presentation alternatives; staff of the Chief Accountant’s Office has provided views regarding pro forma fee tables and capitalization tables to reduce burden and shareholder confusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When multiple potential outcomes exist, consider the SEC staff guidance (IM-DCFO 1995-11) on presenting pro forma fee and capitalization information to avoid undue burden and confusion; multiple alternatives may otherwise be required by strict rule interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a shell company (Reg C Rule 405)
rubrics_metrics.description: A shell company is an entity (other than an asset-backed issuer) that has no or nominal operations and either has: no or nominal assets; assets consisting solely of cash and cash equivalents; or assets consisting of any amount of cash and cash equivalents and nominal other assets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SPACs are an example of shell companies. At the time of the merger (de-SPAC), the SPAC would generally no longer be considered a shell company. See Reg C Rule 405 and KPMG Handbook section references for SPAC accounting guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Predecessor determination for SEC reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Designation of a predecessor is required if a registrant succeeds to substantially all of the business of another entity and the registrant's own operations before the succession appear insignificant relative to the operations assumed or acquired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common scenarios include reverse recapitalization, reverse acquisition with a domestic registrant that is not a shell, and forward mergers. When multiple acquisitions occur, consider relative size and fair value of targets, historical and ongoing management structure, and order of acquisition. Provide robust disclosures of facts and judgments; in limited cases co-predecessors may be appropriate. See FRM citations and 2015 AICPA Conference guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial statement requirements when a predecessor is identified
rubrics_metrics.description: When an acquired business is designated the registrant’s predecessor, S-X Rule 3-05 does not apply; S-X Rules 3-01 and 3-02 apply to determine financial statement requirements for the predecessor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Predecessor financial statements must be full financial statements (abbreviated statements that could satisfy S-X Rule 3-05 cannot be used). Include all periods and dates required by S-X Articles 3 and 10 (or Article 8 for SRCs) with no lapse in audited periods. Include schedules required by S-X Article 12 (e.g., Valuation and Qualifying Accounts). Example timelines: if Target is acquired April 15, registrant must have Target’s entire annual period audited. See FRM references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form 8-K and Form 10 content when reverse recapitalization involves a shell company
rubrics_metrics.description: A reverse recapitalization involving a shell company requires filing a Form 8-K; the SEC staff treats these as capital transactions accounted for as reverse recapitalizations, and Item 2.01(f) of Form 8-K specifies inclusion of all information required in a Form 10 initial registration statement for the private operating company (accounting acquirer).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File the required Form 8-K information no later than four business days after consummation. Item 9.01(c) does not permit a 71-calendar day extension for financial statements or other required information. Include Items such as: Item 2.01 (completed merger), Item 5.01 (change in control), Item 5.06 (material terms), and Item 9.01 (financial statements and pro forma). See FRM references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting when an FPI ceases being a public shell company
rubrics_metrics.description: If an FPI ceases to be a public shell company because of a reverse acquisition or merger, the transaction must be reported on a Form 20-F within four business days of its completion and the Form 20-F includes the financial statements of the other party to the transaction (the legal acquiree).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form 20-F includes the same information as a registration on Form 20-F; the Form 20-F accommodations permitting two years of financial statements instead of three apply. Reports filed during the remainder of the fiscal year may continue under FPI forms; beginning the first day of the following fiscal year, the registrant must use domestic forms and requirements. See Exchange Act Rules and FRM citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial statement periods and age requirements for reverse recapitalizations involving a public shell
rubrics_metrics.description: Form 8-K must include financial statements for all periods required by Reg S-X (as if the operating company were newly registering). S-X Rule 3-06 (9–12 months substitution) does not apply to the accounting acquirer in a reverse recapitalization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The number and age of periods depend on whether the operating company would qualify as an SRC (Article 8: two years permitted) or not (Article 3: two or three years required). If both parties qualify as EGCs and the shell has not filed a first Form 10-K, two years may be permitted; otherwise three years. If initial Form 8-K lacks the most recent completed periods, an amended Form 8-K is required (amendment deadlines for omitted annual period: within 90 days of operating company year-end for non-accelerated filers; for interim period: within 45 days of interim period-end for non-accelerated filers). Registrant must continue filing periodic reports for periods ending before consummation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abbreviated and carve-out financial statements (S-X Rule 3-05 and 3-05(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: When a registrant acquires part of an entity that constitutes a business, it may be able to provide abbreviated (or carve-out) financial statements of the acquired business to comply with S-X Rule 3-05, subject to the rule’s conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the decision tree: if less than substantially all assets are acquired and separate full financial statements exist, consider carve-out statements; if conditions of S-X Rule 3-05(e) are met, abbreviated statements may be acceptable (e.g., statement of assets acquired and liabilities assumed and statement of comprehensive income). Special rules apply for oil and gas properties (see Question 10.3.40–10.3.140). Ensure periods and age match requirements for full statements when abbreviated statements are used; see Question 10.3.80 and related sections for conditions and form/content requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEC staff waivers and remedies when registrant cannot comply with financial statement requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If it is impossible or would involve unreasonable expense and effort to obtain audited financial statements required by S-X Rule 3-05, the SEC staff may waive some financial statement requirements upon written request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Possible staff actions include permitting omission of one or more years of financial statements, issuing a no-action letter (agreeing not to take action solely due to noncompliance), or permitting other accommodations. Factors such as 'unreasonable expense and effort' are considered; see Q&A on waiver requests and examples (waiver request letter, Form S-3 eligibility consequences).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to update and amend initial Form 8-K financial disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-acquisition financial statements included in an initial Form 8-K may need updating if they do not include the operating company’s most recently completed full fiscal year or latest interim period; an amended Form 8-K must be filed to include those periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the omitted most recently completed pre-acquisition period is an annual period, the amended Form 8-K is due within 90 days of the operating company’s year-end for non-accelerated filers; if an interim period, within 45 days of the interim period-end for non-accelerated filers. Ensure the amended filing includes all information that would be in an annual/periodic report (Form 10-K/Form 10-Q) for the operating company.
